name: re-origin
founders: Ben Ahrens (co-founder; AADP holistic health practitioner, ex-personal trainer; self-reported recovery from chronic neurological Lyme/CFS)
Current co-CEOs: Natalie Rivans, Cherrie West
Science advisors ('Brain Trust'): Ken Gorfinkle PhD, Kelly Kent PhD, Martin Alpert MD, Brian Plante ND
founded_year_range: 2020-2021 (estimate). Wayback shows the domain as a parking page in Aug 2018 and Aug 2019 and a full re-origin site (course, Momentum group coaching, team page) by 23 Oct 2021. The site says the Brain Trust formed in 2019; earliest press is Jan 2022. No exact launch date is published.
cost_summary: Program + Community costs USD 379/yr (auto-renew), shown as USD 297 with code HEAL (verified Oct 2026). Group coaching costs USD 279-329 for 10 weekly sessions (USD 329 list, USD 279 discounted; verified Oct 2026). 1:1 coaching price is not public. A conditional results guarantee allows a refund request within 12 months if there is no value after 6 months of daily practice. Free workshops and quizzes serve as a lead-in.
mechanisms: limbic system impairment / amygdala threat conditioning
autonomic/nervous system dysregulation (sympathetic overdrive, "stuck in fight-or-flight")
mechanism_summary: The site's model is "limbic cross-wiring," which it presents as a hypothesis. An acute infection, injury or stressor hits while allostatic load is already high. This creates a Hebbian "neuroimmune association" that conditions the limbic system into a persistent threat response. That response keeps driving the immune, endocrine and autonomic systems ("stuck in fight-or-flight"), producing inflammation, fatigue, pain, sensitivities, anxiety and depression. Benign cues then retrigger it. The proposed fix is repeated self-directed neuroplasticity training plus somatic regulation. One model is applied to all conditions.
techniques: 28-day / 4-week self-paced video course (nervous-system education, retraining techniques, daily application, maintenance)
undisclosed five-step neurocognitive interrupt-and-replace technique using repetition, positive emotion, language and visualization
~30 min/day practice for at least 6 months
follow-along somatic exercises, breathwork, vagus nerve exercises
group coaching (10 weekly Zoom sessions) and 1:1 / somatic coaching by re-origin-certified coaches
graded reintroduction of movement for fatigue
mainstream_notes: Direct-to-consumer only. No health-system, guideline or payer uptake found. Media presence is mostly podcasts and sponsored press releases (Business Insider markets release 2024, NY Weekly), plus a WebMD 2022 brain-fog mention that did not evaluate the program.
insurance_notes: No insurance or HSA/FSA statement found. The annual subscription is paid out of pocket.
controversy: No peer-reviewed evaluation: PubMed returned 0 hits (re-checked 2026-10-12) and there is no ClinicalTrials.gov registration. The /science page shows uncontrolled internal figures (98% improved, 66% pain-free) with no N. Its N=108 6-week pre/post block currently shows 0% placeholders in every field. The /program page cites '200 members' self-report (94% fewer physical symptoms, >82% less anxiety/depression, 88% better QoL). These figures sit beside RCTs of other interventions (PRT: Ashar 2022; MAIR: Sanabria-Mazo 2020), which implies borrowed efficacy. Advisor credentials are inconsistent across pages (Martin Alpert is listed as MD on one page and PhD on another). One limbic model is applied to a very broad list (MCAS, mould, ADHD, OCD, phone addiction). This shares the wider ME/CFS-community criticism of limbic-retraining programs, which are seen as implying symptoms are learned or psychogenic. The founder's 'two decades as a neuroscience researcher' self-description sits beside fitness and holistic-health credentials. There are auto-renewing subscriptions and add-on upsells, and a few Trustpilot complaints about cost and usability.

indicators.value: N=108 (6-week pre/post; results shown as 0% placeholders); separately '200 members' self-report
'hundreds of re-origin's members' (about page, current and Wayback 2023-2025); the ~12,000 participants figure from scoping appears nowhere on the site or its archived home/about pages
~35 condition pages and 50+ articles added Nov-Dec 2025; coach roster ~10 by 2026
'One deep breath', TEDxBushwick, uploaded 2015-05-26; ~41k YouTube views (Oct 2026)

popularity.reach_estimate: ~1,000-10,000 cumulative members (order 10^3). The site has said 'hundreds of members' since at least 2023 and Trustpilot volume is modest; the ~12,000 figure has no public source.
popularity.method_notes: The trajectory is built from: Wayback captures (domain parked Aug 2019; live site by Oct 2021), the site's founding-team date (Brain Trust 2019), press/podcast dates on /press (concentrated in 2022), Trustpilot review dates (from 2023), sitemap lastmod dates (SEO and coaching expansion late 2025-2026), and the leadership change to co-CEOs. Reddit could not be measured (automated access blocked) and Google Trends was not available. reach_log10 was lowered from 3.7 to 3.5 during fact-check, since the only verifiable count statement is 'hundreds of members'.

sources: ClinicalTrials.gov API search 2026-10-12: no re-origin study
